explanation.text:
Upon Alamoth--most probably denotes the treble, or part sung by female voices, the word meaning "virgins"; and which was sung with some appropriately keyed instrument (compare Ch1 15:19-21; see on Psa 6:1, title). The theme may be stated in LUTHER'S well-known words, "A mighty fortress is our God." The great deliverance (Kg2 19:35; Isa 37:36) may have occasioned its composition. (Psa 46:1-11)

refuge--literally, "a place of trust" (Psa 2:12).

strength-- (Psa 18:2).

present help--literally, "a help He has been found exceedingly."

trouble--as in Psa 18:7.

bsb.title: For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. A song.
bsb.text: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble.

explanation.text: The most violent civil commotions are illustrated by the greatest physical commotions.

bsb.text: Therefore we will not fear, though the earth is transformed and the mountains are toppled into the depths of the seas,

explanation.text: swelling--well represents the pride and haughtiness of insolent foes.

bsb.text: though their waters roar and foam and the mountains quake in the surge. Selah

explanation.text:
God's favor is denoted by a river (compare Psa 36:8; Zac 14:8; Rev 22:1).

city of God, the holy place--His earthly residence, Jerusalem and the temple (compare Psa 2:6; Psa 3:4; Psa 20:2; Psa 48:2, etc.). God's favor, like a river whose waters are conducted in channels, is distributed to all parts of His Church.

most High--denoting His supremacy (Psa 17:2).

bsb.text: There is a river whose streams delight the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells.

explanation.text: right early--literally, "at the turn of morning," or change from night to day, a critical time (Psa 30:5; compare Isa 37:36).

bsb.text: God is within her; she will not be moved. God will help her when morning dawns.

explanation.text:
(Compare Psa 46:2).

earth melted--all powers dissolved by His mere word (Psa 75:3; Hos 2:22).

bsb.text: Nations rage, kingdoms crumble; the earth melts when He lifts His voice.

explanation.text:
with us--on our side; His presence is terror to our enemies, safety to us.

refuge--high place (Psa 9:9; compare also Psa 24:6, Psa 24:10).

bsb.text: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah

explanation.text: what desolations--literally, "who hath put desolations," destroying our enemies.

bsb.text: Come, see the works of the LORD, who brings devastation upon the earth.

explanation.text: The usual weapons of war (Psa 7:12), as well as those using them, are brought to an end.

bsb.text: He makes wars to cease throughout the earth; He breaks the bow and shatters the spear; He burns the shields in the fire.

explanation.text:
Be still, etc.--literally, "Leave off to oppose Me and vex My people. I am over all for their safety." (Compare Isa 2:11; Eph 1:22).

Next: Psalms Chapter 47

bsb.text: “Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.”

explanation.text:
The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. See Gill on Psalm 46:7. The Targum paraphrases it, "the Word of the Lord of hosts", as in Psalm 46:7; and the same words are here repeated, to comfort those that were fearful and unbelieving, with which the church then comforted herself.

Selah; on this word; see Gill on Psalm 3:2.

bsb.text: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah
